To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have cloned a rat hepatocyte EP3‐receptor cDNA that is identical with the mouse mastocytomac EP3β‐receptor cDNAs.
we cloned a rat hepatocyte PGE2 receptor of the subtype EP3β and expressed the receptor in HEK 293 and CHO cells.
a cDNA encoding a rat hepatocyte EP3β receptor has been cloned and expressed in mammalian cells and that this EP3β receptor is functionally similar to that of mouse mastocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cloning of functional cDNAs of rat liver EP3‐prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) receptors from a rat liver cDNA library, using a PCR‐strategy.
the isolation of a cDNA clone of a rat hepatocyte PGE2 receptor of the subtype EP3β.
the cloning of functional receptors of the EP1‐, EP2‐ and EP3‐type.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rat hepatocyte EP3‐receptor is identical to the mouse mastocytome EP3β‐receptor.
rat hepatocytes possess an EP3β receptor that inhibits the glucagon‐stimulation of glycogenolysis via inhibition of cAMP.
EP3β receptors are present in rat hepatocytes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EP3‐receptor subtype of rat hepatocytes is identical to the EP3 receptor subtype of mouse mastocyma.
the EP3β‐receptor is the receptor subtype that is expressed in hepatocytes.
the rat hepatocytes possess a single EP3β receptor subtype that is functionally coupled to the inhibition of cAMP formation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rat hepatocytes express a functional EP3 receptor subtype of the β‐type that can be cloned and stably expressed in heterologous cell lines.
rat hepatocytes possess a functional EP3‐receptor subtype that is similar to the EP3‐receptors in mouse mastocytomas and in the rat uterus.
the EP3β receptors in rat hepatocytes and mouse mastocytomas are very closely related.
